chunks: And from him, from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Safwan and Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Asimi, from Ali ibn al-Hasan ibn Faddal, from al-Abbas ibn Amir, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Shu'ayb al-Aqarqufi, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who has a female slave, has intercourse with her, and seeks offspring from her, but is not granted a child from her. So he gifts her to his brother or sells her, and she bears him children. Is it permissible for him to marry the child of his brother from her? He said, 'Repeat it to me.' I repeated it to him. He said, 'There is no harm in it.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a man to marry the child his brother had with a concubine he previously owned?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies the lineage and marital eligibility rules regarding a concubine (*Umm al-Walad*) transferred to a brother. He permits the original owner to marry the child born to the brother from that same woman, establishing that the transfer of the woman does not sever the original owner's right to marry her offspring, provided the child is not his own direct offspring from her. This ruling highlights the flexibility in Shia jurisprudence regarding *Umm al-Walad* status and the distinct legal identities of the woman and her children in cases of sale or gift.
